> buddy mini is a small desk buddy that reacts to me with animated eyes, sounds, and buttons. i want it to feel like a little character sitting on my desk instead of just being another circuit. this is my first step toward building a bigger desk robot that can eventually move around, listen to me, and talk back.

## Design

### 2026-09-30 — spent 2 hours this session planning buddy mini and figuring out how i want the electronics to work.

**2h**

spent 2 hours this session planning buddy mini and figuring out how i want the electronics to work.

i first locked down the v1 features: an animated 128x64 oled face, two buttons, different buzzer sounds, automatic blinking, and a status led. i also decided what i’m leaving out for now, like motors, a battery, a microphone, ai, soldering, and a 3d printed case.

i learned what the main parts actually do instead of just copying a wiring diagram. i looked at how the oled uses i²c, why leds need resistors, how a passive buzzer works, and how the rows and power rails on a breadboard connect.

i then made the block diagram and picked the gpio pins i plan to use: 21 and 22 for the oled, 32 and 33 for the buttons, 25 for the buzzer, and 26 for the led. i also looked into which esp32 pins i should avoid because of boot, flash, or input limitations.

finally, i sketched three faces for buddy: normal, happy, and blink. i kept the eye positions the same and only changed the eye shapes, so the blink can be a simple animation instead of redrawing the whole face.

nothing was built yet since the kit hasn’t arrived, but i now have a much clearer idea of how the parts will connect and what i want buddy mini to look and feel like.
